images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A small desk fan with a brushed graphite cage and frosted acrylic blades, about the height of a mug, sits at the left of a pale neutral tabletop, aimed to the right. In front of it lies a loose stack of ivory paper, edges slightly misaligned. Next to the stack stands a full frosted mug, then a graphite power strip whose cord runs back to the fan. Beyond, a slim graphite wall shelf holding three ivory binders is mounted above a second desk in the right background. The fan's acid-lime power switch is just being clicked on, the only colour in the scene. The top sheet's corner curls up, and fine dust sits on the fan cage. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama, captured mid-disaster. The same objects falling in sequence from left to right. The fan spins, its acid-lime switch on, and the top ivory sheet has lifted and flown into the frosted mug, tipping it. A sheet of grey coffee arcs out onto the graphite power strip, which gives a small pale spark and jerks its cord, yanking the shelf bracket loose. The shelf is caught mid-drop, its three ivory binders tumbling open, the first striking the second desk, which tips onto its side. Loose paper swirls in the fan's draught, droplets hang in the air, and dust and scraps trace a clear line from the last falling desk back to the fan. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A long valley stretches toward a hazy horizon, crossed by a line of giant toppled desks and shelves lying one against the next like fallen dominoes, each the size of a building, weathered, cracked and furred with pale dust. Drifts of ivory paper fill the gaps between them. At the near end, the enormous fan lies on its back, its frosted blades cracked. A colossal mug rests on its side, stained grey inside. The chain runs on down the valley, but in the midground the last desk still stands, leaning only slightly, held by a lime stop block that a slim graphite rail tractor has just pushed into place at its base, bracing it against the fall. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface.
